title: Ordinary Kipping Pull-Up Capacity
subtitle: 3-week kipping capacity block
summary: Two short sessions a week for three weeks. This block trains two separate qualities: set length — how long one set stays clean — and total capacity — how many clean reps a session holds. Forty reps are now inside total capacity, but on 10 August the kip disappeared on rep 40 and strict pulling strength finished it. So the block finishes by buying set length at low volume, then requiring the kip itself to survive all forty, before the applied 50.

primarySkill.title: The one skill this block trains
primarySkill.cue: Same push-away, same tempo, every rep of every set — the last rep of a set of five should look like the first, and the arch after it should still be alive.
primarySkill.failureSignal: When the push-away disappears and the next kip turns arm-dominant, the set is finished. Reps taken after that rehearse the wrong descent and buy nothing but hot spots and sore elbows.

spacingNote: Take at least 48 hours without dynamic pulling before the first session, then keep sessions 48–72 hours apart.

warmup.title: Warm-up — every session
items: 1 easy set of 3 linked kipping pull-ups

sessionRules.title: Rules for every session
items: Skip the extra skill session when the day's WOD already contains roughly 30 or more pulling reps.
Stop a set when the push-away disappears, the next kip turns arm-dominant, pain appears, or a hand hot spot develops.
Move back one step after two rhythm failures, and repeat a session until it is clean.
A prescribed top set is a ceiling, not a test — stop it on the number even when more reps are available.
No butterfly and no chest-to-bar training volume during these three weeks.

progressionRule: Complete each session cleanly before advancing, and repeat a session as often as it takes. Progress is earned by holding the same push-away at the same tempo through the last set — never by the calendar reaching week three.

feedbackPrompt.title: Tell Nabu after each session
items: Which rep the push-away first disappeared on, if any
Any pain or hand hot spots
Did the last set look like the first, or did the final reps turn arm-dominant?

weeks.focus: Make four linked reps ordinary, then take one longer set on purpose rather than discovering it at failure.

A.label: Repeat fours
A.goal: Six identical sets of four, each rep ending in the same push-away back into the arch.

blocks.note: Rest 60 seconds between sets. Same push-away after every rep, including rep four.
The prescription is the ceiling as well as the target — do not add sets because it felt easy.

notes: Scheduled for Tuesday 4 August — the block opens here, so take at least 48 hours without dynamic pulling before it.
If a set breaks rhythm twice, drop to sets of three for the rest of the session and repeat this session next time.

B.label: Controlled six + back-off fives
B.goal: Find out what one longer set costs, at a length chosen in advance instead of discovered at failure.

blocks.note: One set of six, then stop. Six is the prescription, not the maximum — end the set at rep six even if more reps are available.
Rest 75 seconds between all sets, including after the top set. Rep five has to rise off the backswing, not off an extra arm pull.
Set length is what moves this session — 26 reps is barely more than the 24 of session 1, and that is deliberate.

notes: Scheduled for Thursday 6 August, at least 48 hours after session 1.
Set length and total capacity are separate qualities, so only one of them moves here.
If rep six turns arm-dominant, end that set at five and take the back-off sets in fours.

weeks.phase: A forty-rep baseline, then a controlled eight
weeks.focus: Establish what total capacity already holds, then buy set length at the lowest volume that still teaches it.

A.label: Accumulate fives — forty-rep baseline
A.goal: Hold five linked reps on a one-minute clock for eight rounds, and find out where the kip itself actually runs out.

blocks.note: Five linked reps at the top of every minute, EMOM, for eight minutes. Every rep still ends in the same push-away.
A total-capacity baseline, not the quality gate. The gate is week 3 session A.

notes: Completed Monday 10 August: all 40 reps, comfortable from a pulling-strength perspective. The kip disappeared on rep 40 and easy strict pulling finished that rep.
That result proves total pulling capacity at forty and nothing more — dynamic kip and grip endurance, not pulling strength, are now the limiters.

B.label: Controlled eight + back-off fours
B.goal: Expose one deliberately stopped set of eight at the lowest total volume that still teaches set length.

blocks.note: One set of eight, then stop. Do not grind it — end the set the moment the push-away changes, and never rescue it with strict pulling strength.
Rest 75–90 seconds between all sets, including after the top set. Fours rather than fives: Thursday's programmed strict chin-up ladder carries the week's high-volume pulling, not this session.
A ceiling, not a target. Set length is the only quality this session buys, so the volume sits deliberately below the forty already proven.

notes: Scheduled for Wednesday 12 August.
A fresh set of eight is a set-length exposure, not WOD pacing — nothing here says to open a 50-rep workout with eight.
If the top set stops early, run the back-off sets as prescribed rather than making the missing reps up.
Thursday carries the programmed high-volume strict chin-ups and no extra kipping; Friday and Saturday stay kipping-free.

weeks.phase: Prove the kip, then apply it
weeks.focus: Require the same kip rhythm on rep forty as on rep one, then take the fifty-rep application after real recovery.

A.label: Repeat the clean-forty gate
A.goal: Forty reps again — but this time passed only if rep forty is still produced by the same kip rhythm as rep one.

blocks.note: Five linked reps at the top of every minute, EMOM, for eight minutes — the same dose as 10 August. Set eight must look like set one, push-away included.

This session is the gate for the fifty-rep application. It passes only when rep 40 uses the same kip rhythm as rep one; a rep rescued by strict pulling strength does not pass it. Repeat it until it does.

notes: Scheduled for Sunday 16 August, and only if shoulders, elbows, grip, and hands feel normal.

The gap from Wednesday is deliberately longer than the usual 48–72 hours: Thursday's programmed strict chin-up ladder is high-volume pulling, and Friday and Saturday stay kipping-free so the gate is taken fresh.
Two rhythm failures here means repeating this session before the application, not moving on to it.

B.label: Fifty-rep application
B.goal: Fifty clean reps under real pacing — opened below the fresh maximum and downshifted before the rhythm goes.

blocks.note: Open with repeatable fives, not a fresh maximum, and downshift early to fours and then threes before the push-away deteriorates. Small sets held together beat one big set followed by singles.

blocks.movement: Standalone fallback if no WOD arrives
blocks.note: Five linked reps every 90 seconds for ten rounds. Stop the moment the push-away goes — an honest 8 rounds beats a scrappy 10.
This is the capacity the 50-pull-up WOD asks for, taken at workout pace rather than as a fresh-set test.

notes: Take it only after week 3 session A is clean and shoulders, elbows, grip, and hands feel normal — a forty finished by strict pulling strength is not a clean forty.
Do not schedule it inside the 17–21 August FMD. If Sunday 16 August only passes the clean-forty gate, take the application after the FMD and its refeed rather than forcing it into that week.
If any of that is not true, repeat week 3 session A instead and take the application 48–72 hours later.
A programmed 50-rep pull-up workout can be the application itself, once the gate is behind you and the same recovery rules hold.

prerequisites.title: Before you start
mustHave: Four linked kipping pull-ups that repeat across fresh sets
A push-away after every rep, including the last one

repCaps.note: Session volume is prescribed, and it does not climb evenly — 24 in the opening session, 40 at the baseline and again at the gate, a deliberate ceiling of 24 at the set-length exposure, and 50 only at the application. Never add reps beyond the day's prescription because a session felt easy.

stopRules: Sharp shoulder pain or medial (inner) elbow pain
A hand hot spot — stop before it tears
notes: No butterfly and no chest-to-bar work belongs in these three weeks; each has its own gate after the block.
Technique guidance here is not medical advice — your floor coach overrides the app.

wodScaling.title: If the 50-pull-up WOD arrives first
wodScaling.intro: Before the clean-forty gate is passed, a 50-rep pull-up workout is a scaling problem, not a test day. Once it is passed the workout can be the application itself — but it is still paced, never attacked.
points: Tell the coach that total capacity is 8×5 EMOM for 40 reps, but that the kip disappeared on rep 40 and strict strength finished it — so the clean kipping gate is still below forty. Update that after every clean session.
Break from rep one. Never open with a set near failure and then grind out singles.
Open below the fresh maximum. A set of eight in a skill session is a set-length exposure, not a workout pace.
Downshift early — fives to fours to sets of three — before the push-away deteriorates rather than after it has gone.
Scale the total volume or the movement with the coach so the workout keeps its intended time domain.
Stop unassisted reps as soon as the push-away or the shoulder position deteriorates, and finish on the coach's scale.

gates.title: Gates after this block
gates.intro: Neither of these belongs inside the block. Each has a gate that has to be met first.

items.requirement: Introduce as low-volume technique work only once sets of five are routine and 8–10 clean ordinary kipping reps come without a hard final pull.
Reconsider only after roughly 15–20 clean unbroken ordinary kipping pull-ups, and learn it with a coach directly watching the shoulder path.

homeBarSubstitutions.title: Home bar — 80 cm wall clearance
homeBarSubstitutions.intro: The home pull-up bar sits about 80 cm from the wall. That geometry does not give reliable clearance for a full hollow-to-arch swing under fatigue, so a tucked-knee, arm-heavy hybrid is not useful muscle-up technique. Substitute deliberately instead of forcing the kip.
points: Burpee pull-up: take the burpee in open space, move under the bar, then complete the prescribed pull-up reps cleanly.
Metabolic bar-muscle-up substitution: one burpee plus two strict or band-assisted pull-ups, with enough assistance to preserve the workout's intended pace.
Technique substitution: use low-bar, feet-assisted muscle-up transitions only on equipment with adequate clearance, and practise dynamic or jumping muscle-ups on a proper rig.
Hybrid reps taken on this bar are not kipping-technique volume. The 14 burpee double pull-ups of 8 August were 28 extra arm-heavy reps after the capacity work, and they count as neither.

m60Scaling.title: Masters (60+) scaling
m60Scaling.intro: Skill practice and workout scaling are different jobs. Keep them separate.
points: Do not rehearse half-kips under fatigue.
In skill work use the prescribed sets from this block — stop the set the moment the push-away goes.
Default WOD substitution: about 40–50% of the programmed reps as strict pull-ups, in small sets, when that preserves the stimulus.
For high-volume or fast metcons, use the coach's intended scale (ring rows, jumping pull-ups, etc.) rather than turning the workout into strict-pull-up failure work.
Never scale 1:1 from kipping reps to strict reps. Ask the floor coach when the intended stimulus is unclear.
During these three weeks keep extra metcon kipping volume low, so the skill sessions stay the best reps of the week.
